description: Consistency-based MSA (T-Coffee; Notredame, Higgins & Heringa 2000): a primary library of global (Needleman–Wunsch) and local (Smith–Waterman) pairwise alignments weighted by percent identity, extended by the triplet consistency transformation (direct weight + Σ min(W1, W2) over third sequences), then progressively aligned along a guide tree (UPGMA by default; guideTree='nj' = neighbour-joining as in the T-Coffee paper) with the extended-library weights as position-specific scores and zero gap penalties (T-Coffee default). The scoring parameters seed the pairwise library (gapModel='affine': Gotoh global and Smith–Waterman–Gotoh local alignments with gapOpen + k·gapExtend) and define totalScore, the sum of pairs of the result (linear column score, or natural affine costs with gapModel='affine'). distance='clustalw' takes the guide-tree distances from ClustalW 2.1's own pairwise stage.

sequences.description: DNA sequences to align (at least one).

gapOpen.description: Gap-open penalty. Used only with gapModel='affine' (a gap of length k then costs gapOpen + k * gapExtend, Gotoh); ignored by the default linear model.

gapExtend.description: Gap penalty per gap position (linear model: every gap position; affine model: the per-position part of gapOpen + k * gapExtend).

distance.description: Guide-tree distance: 'linear' (default) = 1 - identities / min(length) of the repository's global alignment under the given scores (linear NW, or Gotoh when gapModel='affine'); 'clustalw' = the same formula on ClustalW 2.1's own pairwise stage (affine local Smith-Waterman-Gotoh alignment with its IUB matrix x100 and gap penalties 15 / 6.66, the 'slow' full-DP mode of clustalw -ALIGN; the match/mismatch/gap parameters are then used only for the profile alignment).

gapModel.description: 'linear' (default): every gap position costs gapExtend and gapOpen is ignored; totalScore is the column sum of pairs (gap-gap columns 0). 'affine': gap runs cost gapOpen + k * gapExtend; the pairwise / profile alignments use affine (Gotoh) dynamic programming and totalScore is the sum of pairs with natural affine gap costs (Altschul 1989: each pair of rows is projected out of the alignment, gap-gap columns skipped, every gap run of the projection pays gapOpen once). For two sequences the affine result is an optimal pairwise alignment; for three or more sequences every method is a heuristic.

guideTree.description: Guide-tree method: 'upgma' (default; Sokal & Michener 1958, the Feng-Doolittle / CLUSTAL-1 choice) or 'nj' (neighbour-joining, Saitou & Nei 1987 - ClustalW 2.1's default tree, T-Coffee/Clustal-style; the unrooted NJ tree is rooted and ordered exactly as clustalw does: Tree::reRoot, left subtree first). With distance='clustalw' and guideTree='nj' the tree equals the .dnd file of clustalw -ALIGN. Both are built by the canonical phylogenetics builders.

alignedSequences.description: The aligned rows of the MSA.

consensus.description: Majority-vote consensus of the aligned rows (gaps vote; a nucleotide beats a gap on ties).

totalScore.description: Sum-of-pairs score of the MSA: linear model = column score (match/mismatch from the matrix, residue-gap = gapExtend, gap-gap = 0); gapModel='affine' = natural affine gap costs (every gap run of each pair projection pays gapOpen once).
